pairs.question: Seni' nostri, Dave, fratrem maiorem Chremem nostin?
pairs.derivation: Geta asks Davos whether he knows Chremes, the elder brother of their master; Davos answers 'Quidni?' (why not = of course). Stripped speaker labels {Ge.}/{Da.} and kept the full interrogative for context (so 'fratrem maiorem Chremem' has its referent). Answer ends at the full stop; what follows is Geta's next question 'quid? eiu' gnatum Phaedriam?'.

pairs.question: Quid paedagogus ille qui citharistriam, quid rei gerit?
pairs.derivation: Davos asks how the lyre-girl's tutor is managing; Geta answers 'sic, tenuiter' (so-so, scantily). Stripped speaker labels {Da.}/{Ge.}, the inline verse number 145, and the angle brackets in r<ei> keeping 'rei'. Answer ends at the full stop; what follows is Davos's next question 'non multum habet quod det fortasse?'.

pairs.question: Non multum habet quod det fortasse?
pairs.derivation: Davos asks whether the tutor perhaps has much he could give; Geta answers 'immo nil nisi spem meram' (no, nothing but sheer hope). Stripped speaker labels {Da.}/{Ge.} and inline verse number 145. Answer is Geta's complete reply; what follows is Davos's next question about the father's return.

pairs.question: Pater eius rediit an non?
pairs.derivation: Davos asks whether his (Phaedria's) father has returned; Geta answers 'nondum' (not yet). Stripped speaker labels {Da.}/{Ge.} and the angle brackets in ei(u)s keeping 'eius'. What follows is Davos's next question 'quid? senem quoad exspectatis vostrum?'.

pairs.question: Adduxtin tecum filiam?
pairs.derivation: Demipho asks Chremes whether he brought his daughter back from Lemnos; Chremes answers 'non' (no). Stripped speaker labels {De.}/{Ch.}; the preceding clause 'Quid? qua profectu' causa hinc es Lemnum, Chreme' is the lead-in, but the discrete interrogative answered by 'non' is 'adduxtin tecum filiam?', so the question is limited to it. What follows is Demipho's next question 'quid ita non?'.

pairs.question: Quid illi tam diu quaeso igitur commorabare, ubi id audiveras?
pairs.derivation: Demipho asks why Chremes lingered so long once he had heard the news; Chremes answers 'pol me detinuit morbus' (illness detained me). Stripped speaker labels {De.}/{Ch.} and inline verse number 570. The discourse particles 'quaeso igitur' are part of Demipho's own utterance, not a speech tag, so kept contiguous. Answer ends at the full stop; what follows is Demipho's clipped question 'unde? aut qui?'.

pairs.question: Duasne uxores habet?
pairs.answer: Au obsecro, unam illequidem hanc solam.
pairs.derivation: Chremes asks whether Antipho has two wives; Sophrona answers that he has only this one. Stripped speaker labels {Ch.}/{So.}; the bare exclamation 'quid?' preceding the interrogative is dropped as Chremes's own framing interjection. 'au obsecro' is part of Sophrona's reply (an interjection, not a tag), so kept. What follows is Chremes's next question 'quid illam alteram quae dicitur cognata?'.

pairs.question: Quid ait tandem?
pairs.derivation: Demipho asks what Nausistrata said about taking the girl away; Chremes answers 'abduci non potest' (she cannot be led away). Stripped speaker labels {De.}/{Ch.}. What follows is Demipho's next question 'qui non potest?'.

pairs.question: Qui non potest?
pairs.derivation: Demipho asks why she cannot be led away; Chremes answers 'quia uterque utrique est cordi' (because each is dear to the other). Stripped speaker labels {De.}/{Ch.} and inline verse number 800. What follows is Demipho's next question 'quid istuc nostra?'.
